resources.string: Your head unit cannot read its own Wi‑Fi address — Android hides it from apps. This phone can see it, so this app looks it up and hands it over.\n\nOpen Settings › Wi‑Fi Setup on the head unit, and make sure Android Auto is not connected.
Looking… this takes about half a minute.
Which one is the head unit?
No paired Bluetooth devices. Pair the head unit with this phone first.
Handing the address over… (%1$s)\n\nEach step can take up to half a minute.
This is its Wi‑Fi Direct network. Hand the address over below, or type it into the head unit yourself.
Could not see the head unit
This phone looked both of the ways it can and did not find the head unit\'s network. Check that:
the head unit is switched on
its Settings › Wi‑Fi Setup screen is open
The closest thing this phone saw was %1$s (%2$s).
A long shot. The head unit can also recognise itself by its Wi‑Fi Direct device name, which this phone cannot read as a network name — so it is worth one try before giving up.
The head unit stored the address and should connect on its own now.
cached — Android refused a new sweep
Done. The head unit stored %1$s and should connect on its own now.
Sent, but the head unit did not recognise anything this phone saw. Search again — while it waits, the head unit renames its network every few seconds, so what this phone read may already be stale.
This app needs location and nearby‑devices permission. Android requires it to read Wi‑Fi networks; nothing is stored or sent anywhere else.
Turn on Location in your phone settings. Android returns no Wi‑Fi networks while it is off.
Turn on Wi‑Fi on this phone so it can see the head unit\'s network.
Bluetooth is off, so the address cannot be handed over. Turn it on and try again, or type the address into the head unit by hand.
The head unit is not listening. Open Settings › Wi‑Fi Setup on it and try again.
Lost the Bluetooth connection to the head unit. Try again, or type the address into the head unit by hand.
Do this once, with the head unit and this phone next to each other. It takes about five minutes.
Open CEONIX Headunit on the head unit. Allow every card on the first screen, tap %1$s, then accept the safety notice.
On the head unit, open Android\'s Bluetooth settings and tap Pair new device. On this phone, choose the head unit in the Bluetooth list and confirm the same code on both screens.
On the head unit\'s home screen, press %1$s and choose this phone. Nothing appears yet, and that is expected: the head unit is setting up its own Wi‑Fi network.
On the head unit, open %1$s › %2$s. Leave that screen open while it says %3$s.
Close this guide, tap %1$s and allow what it asks for. The search takes about half a minute.
When the card says %1$s, tap %2$s and choose the head unit in the list.
This phone says %1$s. Android Auto then connects on its own; if it does not, press %2$s on the head unit once. The very first time, accept the Android Auto prompts on this phone.
